summary: Hot CPI reset the trade. The October inflation report ran +0.4% on the month against the +0.3% the market expected, and the reaction was textbook. Rate-cut odds got trimmed and gold took the hit, crashing 2.7% to 4,039 and losing the trailing stop it reclaimed yesterday. Equities wobbled but did not break. The Nasdaq slipped 0.6% to 27,836 and the S&P eased 0.4% to 7,544. Both lost their trailing stops (a volatility line, above it favors longs), yet both closed back inside the day's range instead of breaking down. VIX spiked to 21.3 on the print then settled under 20 at 19.6, so the fear was brief. Crude kept sliding to 86.31, still short below its stop. Yesterday's confirmed up-trend is on hold now, not broken: the stops flipped, but the equity selling stayed mild and contained.

risk.note: Stepped down from NORMAL because both equity boards lost their trailing stops after a hot October CPI (+0.4% vs +0.3%), even though volatility stayed contained (VIX under 20, ATR eased). Keep size down until the stops settle on one side. Week ahead: Veterans Day Wednesday Nov 11 (bond market closed, equity futures open); next policy event the December FOMC.

psychology: The hard part today was sitting still. One inflation number flipped the stops that had confirmed a trend only a day earlier, and that tempts two mistakes: buying the dip on faith the up-trend resumes, or chasing the gold-style collapse into an equity short. A single print that moves your stops is information, not a reason to overtrade. When price closes back inside the opening range on an event day, the market is telling you it has not decided. The edge is patience. Let the stops rebuild a direction before you commit size, and do not let the gold crash scare you into an equity short the tape does not support.
